revenue_growth.source: Assumption: decelerating from FY2025 growth of 22.2% (200,966/164,501) as the base gets larger; fading toward terminal growth.

ebit_margin.source: Assumption: slightly below FY2025 margin of 41.4% (83,276/200,966) to reflect rising depreciation from heavy AI capex.

tax_rate.source: Assumption: normalized rate below the 21% US statutory rate, reflecting Meta's historically lower effective rate; the FY2025 rate (about 30%, from pretax 85,932 and net income 60,458) looks inflated by a one-off tax charge, so I excluded it.

da_pct_revenue.source: Assumption: FY2025 was 9.3% (18,616/200,966) and FY2024 was 9.4%; raised to 10% as the FY2025 capex step-up depreciates.

capex_pct_revenue.source: Assumption: FY2025 was 34.7% (69,691/200,966) and FY2024 was 22.6%; assume intensity eases from the FY2025 peak but stays well above the FY2024 level.

wacc.source: Assumption anchored on Damodaran US Software (Internet) cost of capital of 10.66% (dataset 2026-01-05). Cross-check: risk-free rate 4.86% (US Treasury 10Y, 2026-11-06) and US ERP 4.46% (Damodaran, 2026-02-16). I rounded down because Meta is a large, cash-rich company with low leverage.

terminal_growth.source: Assumption: below the 4.86% risk-free rate and near long-run nominal GDP growth.

net_debt.source: financial_statements META derived net_debt = total debt 58,744 - cash 35,873 - marketable securities 45,719, accession 0001628280-26-003942 (excludes leases)
